title: Heartbeat-anchored incremental recovery for streaming responses
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Add a heartbeat-anchored incremental recovery mechanism to the streaming output stack. Currently clients that disconnect must either re-request the full response or rely on coarse resume tokens that force servers to resend large segments. The proposed approach embeds lightweight heartbeat anchors in the SSE stream that include an ordered anchor id, the last-ack'd chunk index, and semantic boundary hints (e.g., function-call-open, function-call-close, json-escape-safe). On reconnect the client presents the last-received anchor id; server can then fast-forward or replay minimal deltas, resume KV-cache offsets, and avoid re-emitting completed function calls or partial structured output constructs. This reduces duplicate tokens, improves tail-latency for reconnect clients, and keeps tool/function-call boundaries intact when partial outputs were received.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server emits heartbeat anchors at configurable intervals (default 1s) with stable schema. 2) Clients can request resume using anchor id header/param and receive a compact replay containing only missing chunks. 3) Function-call and structured-output boundaries must not be duplicated — resumed stream either completes an open call or atomically rewinds to previous safe boundary. 4) Backwards compatibility: legacy clients using resume-token continue to work via compatibility shim. 5) End-to-end tests validate idempotency and ordering for simulated disconnects across 0.5s-10s outages. 6) Telemetry surfaced in Console showing anchor frequency, recovered-by-anchor rate, and bytes saved on resume.
design_notes:
- Heartbeat anchor format: base64 JSON with {anchor_id, seq_index, boundary_hint, kv_cache_offset, signature}. Signature uses per-connection short HMAC to detect divergence.
- Probe negotiation: new header X-Redwood-Stream-Resume: 'anchor'|'token'|'none' negotiates server/client preference.
- Boundary semantics: treat function-call-open as unsafe rewind point unless function-call-close seen; in that case resume may omit replay.
- Server optimization: maintain per-connection compact chunk catalog (sliding window) to serve delta replays without full recomputation.
- Telemetry: emit anchors_emitted, anchors_used_for_resume, avg_replay_bytes, duplicate_token_rate.
- Security: anchor signature avoids accidental cross-connection replays; ensure HMAC rotates on reconnection where auth changes.
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Thompson: Initial ticket created after incident #INC-2025-56 where a disconnected client re-request caused 3x token duplication during peak. Proposed heartbeat anchor approach to reduce cost and tail latency.

2025-02-14 Ravi Patel: Spike completed. Implemented prototype at runtime/stream/anchor-spike branch. Prototype emits anchors every 1s and server maintains last 30s chunk catalog. Observed 45% reduction in bytes sent on short reconnects. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7123

2025-02-17 Design Review (Lena Gao): Agreed on boundary_hint enum values: 'atomic', 'func_open', 'func_close', 'json_safe'. Recommended adding explicit field for 'structured_root' to help SDKs rehydrate partial JSON outputs.

2025-02-18 Security Review (Omar Ruiz): Raised concern about anchor reuse across credentials. Decision: anchors include connection-scoped nonce and HMAC derived from connection token; rotation on every auth change required.

2025-02-19 Ravi Patel: Implemented negotiation header X-Redwood-Stream-Resume and compatibility shim for legacy resume-token flow. Compatibility case translates token -> synthetic anchor on server side for older clients.

2025-02-21 QA (Anika Bose): Integration tests added. Simulated reconnect matrix: durations [0.3s, 1s, 3s, 7s]. Verified no duplicate function calls in 98/100 runs; two failures traced to ambiguous boundary_hint when chunk split occurred mid-utf8 codepoint — added chunk-alignment step on emitter.

2025-02-24 Observability (SRE): Added dashboard 'Streaming / Anchor Recovery' with panels for anchors_emitted/min, anchors_used_pct, replay_bytes_saved. Early signals show anchors_used_pct ~ 12% in canary tenant and avg_replay_bytes_saved ~ 28KB per resume.

2025-02-25 PM (Renee Kim): Please ensure SDKs expose an api to automatically supply last anchor on reconnect and a fallback to token-based resume for older SDK versions. Add migration note in console release notes.

2025-02-26 Ravi Patel: Working on end-to-end tests for tool-calling edge cases (nested calls, split-function-call frames). Next: stabilize HMAC rotation, add gate flag runtime.feature.anchor_recovery default=false for initial rollout.

Links: Design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Heartbeat+Anchors+Design, Implementation spike PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7123, Canaries: dashboard link https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/stream-anchor
